brief: Goldman forecasts October core CPI up 0.16% month-over-month seasonally adjusted, below the 0.2% consensus, and headline CPI up 0.21% (vs. 0.3% consensus) as higher food and energy prices offset easing elsewhere; the forecast implies a larger 0.23% increase in core PCE. Year-over-year comparisons are unavailable for most indexes because October 2025 data is missing from last year's government shutdown; Goldman's first available comparison, for November, projects headline CPI accelerating to 3.81% y/y (from 3.74% in September) and core CPI to 2.67% (from 2.56%). Three component drivers: airfares flat month-over-month on tracked online prices; health insurance down 2.5% as a semiannual source-data update turns the series deeply negative for six months, with no PCE impact because PCE sources that component differently; and autos cooling as used car prices fall 1.5%, new cars rise 0.1%, and auto insurance falls 0.3%. BLS's method for backfilling the shutdown-era data gap (geometric mean of September and November 2025) introduces residual seasonality Goldman estimates adds 5bp to October's seasonally-adjusted core reading, concentrated in public transportation, apparel, and hotels. Goldman expects core CPI near 0.1% monthly in November and December as shelter slows further.

cards.claim: Goldman forecasts October core CPI to rise 0.16% month-over-month seasonally adjusted, below the 0.2% consensus estimate.
cards.anchor: We expect a 0.16% increase in October core CPI (vs. +0.2% consensus).

cards.claim: Goldman forecasts October headline CPI to rise 0.21% month-over-month seasonally adjusted, below the 0.3% consensus estimate, driven by higher food and energy prices.
cards.anchor: We expect a 0.21% increase in headline CPI (vs. +0.3% consensus), reflecting higher food (+0.4%) and energy (+0.5%) prices.

cards.claim: Goldman's CPI forecast implies a larger 0.23% monthly increase in core PCE for October.
cards.anchor: Our forecast is consistent with a larger 0.23% monthly increase in core PCE in October

cards.claim: Year-over-year comparisons are unavailable for most CPI indexes, including headline and core, because October 2025 values are missing due to last year's government shutdown.
cards.anchor: Year-over-year calculations will not be available for most indexes, including the headline and core CPIs, reflecting missing values for October 2025 due to last year’s government shutdown that hampered data collection.

cards.claim: Goldman forecasts November headline CPI to accelerate to a 3.81% year-over-year increase, up from 3.74% in September.
cards.anchor: we forecast a 3.81% increase in headline CPI (vs. 3.74% in September)

cards.claim: Goldman forecasts November core CPI to accelerate to a 2.67% year-over-year increase, up from 2.56% in September.
cards.anchor: 2.67% increase in core CPI (vs. 2.56%)

cards.claim: Goldman expects the CPI airfares component to be unchanged month-over-month in October, based on its tracking of online airfare prices.
cards.anchor: We expect the airfares component to be unchanged month-over-month, reflecting the signal from our equity analysts’ tracking of online price data.

cards.claim: CPI airfares have risen 2.5% per month on average so far this year, reflecting the sharp increase in oil and refined product prices.
cards.anchor: The component has increased by 2.5% per month on average so far this year as a result of the sharp increase in oil and refined product prices.

cards.claim: Goldman expects CPI health insurance prices to fall 2.5% in October as a semiannual source-data update turns the component meaningfully negative for the next six months.
cards.anchor: we expect the upcoming update to result in meaningfully negative readings over the next six months (we assume -2.5% for October)

cards.claim: Goldman does not expect the health insurance source-data update to affect core PCE inflation, since PCE sources health and auto insurance data differently than CPI.
cards.anchor: source data in the PCE index, so we do not expect this update to affect PCE inflation.

cards.claim: Goldman expects CPI used car prices to decline 1.5% in October, based on the signal from used car auction prices.
cards.anchor: a 1.5% decline in used car prices, based on the signal from used car auction prices

cards.claim: Goldman expects CPI new car prices to rise 0.1% in October, reflecting negative residual seasonality.
cards.anchor: a 0.1% increase in new car prices, reflecting negative residual seasonality

cards.claim: Goldman expects CPI auto insurance prices to decline 0.3% in October, reflecting a modest decline in premiums indicated by its online dataset.
cards.anchor: a 0.3% decline in auto insurance prices, reflecting a modest decline in premiums indicated by our online dataset

cards.claim: Goldman estimates that residual seasonality from the BLS's shutdown-era data interpolation will add an unwarranted 5 basis points to October's seasonally-adjusted core CPI, concentrated in public transportation, apparel, and hotels.
cards.anchor: estimate that this new source of residual seasonality will unduly boost October seasonally-adjusted core CPI inflation by 5bp

cards.claim: Goldman forecasts more moderate shelter increases in October, with owners' equivalent rent up 0.26% and rent of primary residence up 0.23%, following last month's jump.
cards.anchor: we forecast more moderate increases in the shelter categories—a 0.26% increase in the OER category and a 0.23% increase in the rent category—following last month’s jump

cards.claim: Core PCE's larger forecast increase than core CPI partly reflects the lower weight of used cars, where Goldman expects a meaningful price decline, in the PCE basket.
cards.anchor: partly reflecting the lower weight of used cars in core PCE (we expect a meaningful decline in used car prices)

cards.claim: Goldman expects the PCE source data for airfares, auto insurance, and health insurance to show increases in October, unlike the CPI source data for those same components.
cards.anchor: and differing source data for airfares, auto insurance, and health insurance—for which we expect the PCE source data to show increases.

cards.claim: Goldman expects the PCE airfares component, which lags CPI airfares because PCE prices flights at consumption while CPI prices them at purchase, to rise further toward the level implied by CPI.
cards.anchor: to increase as it moves further toward the level implied by its CPI equivalent

cards.claim: Goldman expects monthly core CPI increases of around 0.1% in November and December, reflecting a continued slowdown in shelter categories.
cards.anchor: we expect monthly core CPI increases of around 0.1% in November and December, reflecting the continued slowdown in the shelter categories

cards.claim: The BLS reran seasonal adjustment by approximating the missing October 2025 index values, caused by the government shutdown, as the geometric mean of the September 2025 and November 2025 index values.
cards.anchor: the BLS approximating missing Oct. 2025 data due to the government shutdown by taking the geometric mean of Sept. 2025 and Nov. 2025 index values
